statement_record.book: For a presheaf P : C^op ⟶ Sets the category of elements ∫_C P has objects the pairs (x, C) with C ∈ C and x ∈ P(C); an arrow h : (x',C') → (x,C) is an arrow h : C' → C of C with P(h)(x) = x'; identities and composition are inherited from C; it is small when C is; the projection π : ∫_C P ⟶ C sends (x,C) ↦ C and an arrow triple to its underlying h.

evidence.intree_statement: Class SubobjectClassifier := { Ω : C; truth : 1 ~> Ω; char {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : x ~> Ω; char_pullback {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one; char_unique {u x : C} (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) (h : x ~> Ω) : IsPullback h truth u m one → h ≈ char m M }.  (* Section context: Context {C : Category}. Context `{HT : @Terminal C}. Context `{HP : @HasPullbacks C}. *)

Theorem classifier_classifies (x : C) : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := SubObj x |} {| carrier := x ~> Ω |}.  (* to := char, from := sub_reindex h truth_subobject, round trips by classifier_char_roundtrip / classifier_pullback_roundtrip *)

statement_record.book: In a category E with all finite limits, a subobject classifier is an object Ω with an arrow t : 1 ⟶ Ω (a universal subobject, i.e. mono) such that for every object E and every mono U ↣ E there is a UNIQUE u : E ⟶ Ω making the square U → 1, U ↣ E, t : 1 → Ω, u : E → Ω a pullback (display 8.6); u is the characteristic arrow of U ↣ E.
statement_record.intree: Class SubobjectClassifier := { Ω : C; truth : 1 ~> Ω; char (m : u ~> x) (M : Monic m) : x ~> Ω; char_pullback : IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one; char_unique (h : x ~> Ω) : IsPullback h truth u m one → h ≈ char m M }.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same. The book's 'there is a unique u' is split, as usual in a proof-relevant setting, into the operation `char` plus `char_unique` (uniqueness up to the hom-setoid ≈, the library's faithful stand-in for equality of arrows), and the square `IsPullback (char m M) truth u m one` is literally display 8.6 with the leg U → 1 taken to be the canonical `one`. Ambient hypotheses are Terminal + HasPullbacks rather than 'all finite limits' — these are exactly the finite-limit data the definition consumes, and terminal + pullbacks generate all finite limits. Two book side-remarks come out as in-tree lemmas rather than assumptions: truth is monic (truth_monic, line 64, derived) and char respects the subobject equivalence (char_respects, line 143, derived rather than a class field).

statement_record.book: A subobject classifier is unique up to isomorphism, because the defining pullback condition is exactly the requirement that the subobject functor Sub_E(−) : E^op ⟶ Sets be representable, with a natural isomorphism Sub_E(−) ≅ Hom_E(−, Ω); the classifying-arrow bijection IS that natural isomorphism, and uniqueness follows from uniqueness of representing objects.
statement_record.intree: classifier_classifies (x : C) : SubObj x ≅ (x ~> Ω) in Sets; Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets; univ_property_unique_up_to_unique_iso.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the classification bijection is proved only OBJECTWISE (one Sets-isomorphism per x), never assembled into an isomorphism of presheaves Sub ≅ [Hom ─, Ω] in [C^op, Sets]; the generic uniqueness-of-representing-objects proposition therefore cannot be invoked, and no uniqueness statement about Ω itself is made.

gap: Three precise shortfalls. (i) Naturality in x of `classifier_classifies` is never proved — there is no lemma relating char (sub_reindex f s) to char s ∘ f — so the family of Sets-isos is not exhibited as a morphism, let alone an isomorphism, in the functor category, and `Sub` is never connected to `[Hom ─, Ω]`. (ii) The in-tree `Representable` class (Functor/Representable.v:46) is COVARIANT only (`F : C ⟶ Sets` with `represented : [Hom repr_obj,─] ≅ F`), so the presheaf `Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets` cannot be declared an instance of it without first passing to C^op, which is not done; likewise `IsUniversalProperty` is never instantiated at the subobject-classifier predicate, so `univ_property_unique_up_to_unique_iso` is never applied here. (iii) No lemma asserts that two subobject classifiers on the same C have isomorphic Ω (rg -n -i 'classifier.*uniq|Omega.*uniq' returns 0 hits).

evidence.intree_statement: Class ElementaryTopos (C : Category) := { topos_terminal : @Terminal C; topos_cartesian : @Cartesian C; topos_pullbacks : @HasPullbacks C; topos_closed : @Closed C topos_cartesian; topos_classifier : @SubobjectClassifier C topos_terminal }.

statement_record.book: A topos is a category E such that (1) E has all finite limits, (2) E has a subobject classifier (Definition 8.15), and (3) E has all exponentials (is cartesian closed).
